title: Trainability and Mode Separation of Mixed IQP-QCBMs
abstract: Quantum circuit Born machines (QCBMs) based on instantaneous quantum polynomial-time (IQP) circuits are promising quantum generative models for their classical trainability. It is known that their ancilla-free form avoids barren plateaus under certain initializations, but remains non-universal. Although adding ancilla qubits raises the expressivity, whether the ancilla-extended model retains local trainability remains unknown. We propose the mixed IQP-QCBM, which generalizes the ancilla-extended circuit as a weighted mixture of ancilla-free IQP circuits, called branches. For a polynomial number of branches, we prove local barren-plateau avoidance from data-agnostic and, under certain assumptions, data-dependent initializations. We further show that the mixed IQP-QCBM can surpass the best ancilla-free IQP circuit only if its branches generate a number of distinct distributions. In particular, we focus on a behavior we call \emph{mode separation}, in which each branch captures a particular feature of the target. Mode separation is hard to attain from an initialization whose branches generate the same distribution: the gradients that would separate them are suppressed while the distributions they generate remain close. This motivates \emph{cluster initialization}, which assigns a different unsupervised data cluster to each branch and provides an initial degree of mode separation. Exact calculations on two 16-bit datasets support the barren-plateau and gradient-suppression claims. On four benchmarks, binary clusters, a two-dimensional Ising model, binarized MNIST, and a 484-spin glass, cluster initialization converges fastest and reaches the lowest mean test $\mathrm{MMD}^2$. We observe that, when achieving the lowest test $\mathrm{MMD}^2$, the mixed IQP-QCBM contains branches specialized to distinguishable data features such as blob patterns, magnetization sectors, or digit shapes.
summary: The paper proposes the mixed IQP-QCBM, an advanced quantum generative model designed for classical trainability. It demonstrates that achieving high fidelity requires 'mode separation,' which is best achieved using a cluster initialization scheme. This approach successfully trains the model to accurately reproduce complex data distributions found in areas like spin glasses and image recognition.
main_problem: The research addresses developing quantum generative models (QCBMs) that are classically trainable while maintaining high expressive power, specifically focusing on the trainability and mode separation capabilities of mixed IQP-QCBMs.
main_result: Cluster initialization significantly outperforms other methods by providing initial mode separation, allowing the model to converge fastest and achieve the lowest test MMD^2 across various complex datasets like spin glasses and MNIST.
method: The authors analyze training using the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) loss function, which is formulated as a weighted sum of squared Pauli-Z correlator mismatches between the model and data moments.
model_or_system: The core model is the mixed IQP-QCBM, an extension of Quantum Circuit Born Machines built from Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-Time (IQP) circuits. It models the probability distribution as a weighted mixture over multiple 'branches,' each derived from an ancilla-free IQP circuit.
key_observables: Test MMD^2 (Mean/Peak), Pauli-Z Correlators ($z_A(	heta)$), and Branch Diversity ($D_{	ext{branch}}$).
important_parameters: The number of branches ($L$), the structure of the weights ($\pi_\ell$), and initialization schemes (data-agnostic, global, cluster).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the IQP circuit is 2-body, and that local barren plateau avoidance can be proven under specific initializations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mechanism of mode separation in QCBMs, contrasting coincident branches (suppressed gradients) with mode-separated branches (allowing open gradient flow).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the mixed IQP-QCBM structure, proves local barren plateau avoidance for this model, and then empirically compares initialization strategies—particularly highlighting cluster initialization's success in achieving mode separation on benchmark datasets.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum machine learning with statistical physics by applying highly structured quantum circuits (IQP) to model complex classical distributions found in disordered systems like spin glasses. The focus on 'mode separation' is a key concept for understanding how deep generative models capture distinct physical features.

Under the corresponding conditions of Sec. III, each initialization shown is locally trainable. (a) At uniform weights, tracing out the ancillas of Uanc-IQP(θ) yields L ancilla-free branches, each weighted by 1/L. (b) Data-agnostic and global initialization are branch-coincident, so their separating gradient vanishes. (c) Cluster initialization assigns different data clusters to the branches, giving distinct starting distributions and noncanceling separating gradients.
